gloss: not at all, not a bit (with negative)

definitions.gloss: not at all, not a bit, not in the least (with negative)
definitions.explanation: Used with negative predicates to emphasize complete absence or negation. Expresses stronger negation than あまり.

examples.japanese: ちっとも⟦{分|わ}からない→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
ちっとも⟦{変|か}わっていない→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}しても→練習：05323_renshuu⟧、ちっとも⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: No matter how many times I practice, I don't get any better at all.

examples.japanese: ⟦{説明|せつめい}→説明：01449_setsumei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦のに→のに：10529_noni⟧、ちっとも⟦{納得|なっとく}→納得：03507_nattoku⟧⟦できなかった→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Even though I heard the explanation, I wasn't convinced at all.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧⟦のに→のに：10529_noni⟧、ちっとも⟦{反省|はんせい}していない→反省：03570_hansei⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: Even though he's in the wrong, he isn't reflecting on it at all, so the people around him are having a hard time too.

notes:
ちっとも is an emphatic negative adverb meaning "not at all" or "not one bit." It must always be paired with a negative predicate.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Pattern: ちっとも + negative verb/adjective
- Cannot be used with positive statements
- Example: ちっとも⟦{分|わ}からない→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧ (I don't understand at all)

USAGE:
Expresses the speaker's frustration, surprise, or emphasis about the complete absence of something. Slightly more emotional than ⟦{全然|ぜんぜん}→全然：00598_zenzen⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{全然|ぜんぜん}→全然：00598_zenzen⟧〜ない: not at all (most common, neutral)
- ちっとも〜ない: not at all (emphatic, slightly emotional)
- ⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧も〜ない: not even a little (emphatic)
- ⟦{全|まった}く→全く：02363_mattaku⟧〜ない: not at all (formal/literary)

REGISTER:
Casual to neutral. More common in spoken language than formal writing. Often used when the speaker is frustrated or disappointed — e.g., ちっとも⟦{上達|じょうたつ}→上達：03346_joutatsu⟧しない (I'm not improving at all).
